plugins.name: @denext/auth
plugins.title: @denext/auth
plugins.blurb: First-party auth for denext, as one opt-in plugin: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC providers, credentials, magic links and one-time codes, passkeys, TOTP second factors, SAML 2.0 SSO, bearer API tokens, revocable…

id.description: URL-safe provider id (the `[provider]` route segment), e.g. `"google"`.

type.description: `"oidc"` verifies an `id_token`; `"oauth"` calls a userinfo endpoint.

userinfoUrl.description: Userinfo endpoint (OAuth providers, or OIDC when you prefer userinfo).

userEmailsUrl.description: Optional endpoint returning the account's email list (e.g. GitHub `/user/emails`), fetched with the access token after userinfo. Its result is passed to profile as `emails`, so the mapper can pick a *verified* address rather than trusting an unverified `userinfo.email`.

jwksUrl.description: JWKS URL for id_token signature keys (OIDC).

profile.description: Map the token/userinfo/claims result to a normalized AuthUser.

tokenEndpointAuthMethod.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint (RFC 6749 §2.3.1). `"client_secret_post"` (the default) sends `client_id` / `client_secret` in the form body; `"client_secret_basic"` sends them as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header instead, which some providers (X, Zoom, Notion) require.

responseMode.description: How the provider returns the authorization response (OAuth 2.0 Multiple Response Type Encoding Practices §2.1). `"query"` (the default) redirects back with `?code=…&state=…`, answered by `GET {basePath}/callback/:id`. `"form_post"` (OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response Mode §2) has the browser POST them as a form to the same URL, which Sign in with Apple requires to hand over a user's name and email. A form_post flow's transaction cookie is `SameSite=None; Secure` — the provider's cross-site POST must carry it — and its callback accepts only the POST: a GET carrying a code is refused.

checks.description: The protections the flow runs besides `state`, as Auth.js's provider `checks` name them. Unset (the default): PKCE (S256), plus a `nonce` for an `"oidc"` provider. Set: PKCE only when the list has `"pkce"`, and a `nonce` only for an `"oidc"` provider whose list has `"nonce"` — for a provider that refuses a `code_verifier` it didn't ask for (`["state"]`). `state` is sent and verified on every flow whatever the list says: `"state"` and `"none"` change nothing about it.

tokenRequestParams.description: Extra form parameters on the token request (TikTok's `client_key`). They never replace one the flow sets itself (`grant_type`, `code`, `redirect_uri`, `code_verifier`, the client credentials).

userinfoRequest.description: Read the profile with a request of the provider's own shape instead of a `GET` of `userinfoUrl` with the access token as a Bearer header (a `POST`, API-key headers, an id from the token response in the URL). `fetch` is the provider fetch, pinned to its hosts.

idTokenAlg.description: `"HS256"`: the provider signs its `id_token` with HMAC-SHA256 under the client secret, as its specification requires (LINE). It is verified with the secret, and no other algorithm is accepted. Unset: the issuer's JWKS (RS / PS / ES algorithms).

allowedHosts.description: Hosts `safeFetch` may reach for this provider (token/userinfo/jwks). Derived from the configured endpoints when omitted. A `*.domain` entry admits that domain's subdomains (not the apex), for an endpoint discovery finds on a per-tenant subdomain.

discovery.description: Fill the endpoints from the provider's OIDC discovery document (`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`) instead of hard-coding them. The fetched document must declare exactly this `issuer` or it is refused, and the request is pinned to the issuer's host.

strictAudience.description: Refuse an `id_token` whose `aud` lists audiences besides this client unless it also carries an `azp` naming this client (RFC 7519 §4.1.3 / OIDC Core §3.1.3.7 step 4). Defaults to **on**; set `false` only for a provider that legitimately mints multi-audience tokens without `azp`.

tenantIssuer.description: A multi-tenant issuer (`microsoftEntra({ tenant: "common" | "organizations" })`): `issuer` is a template carrying `{tenantid}`, and an `id_token` is accepted only when its `iss` is exactly that template with the token's own tenant claim (`claim`, a GUID) substituted — the templated issuer the provider's discovery document declares. `allowedTenants` limits which tenants may sign in; `excludedTenants` refuses some (`organizations` excludes the personal-account tenant).

claim.description: The claim naming the token's tenant (Microsoft Entra: `tid`). Its value must be a GUID.

allowedTenants.description: Only these tenants (GUIDs) may sign in; unset admits every tenant.

excludedTenants.description: These tenants (GUIDs) may never sign in.

allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking.description: DANGEROUS: when this provider returns an email that already belongs to a local account, link to it even though that account's address is **unverified**. Off by default, and off is the safe answer — an attacker who registers an unverified local account with a victim's address would otherwise take it over at the victim's first provider login.

type.description: Discriminant marking this as a credentials provider.

authorize.description: Validate submitted credentials and return the user, or `null` to reject. MUST NOT leak whether an account exists (return `null` for an unknown account and a wrong password alike) and must compare passwords in constant time — store hashes from `hashPassword` and check with `verifyPassword` (both from `denext/server`). Failed attempts are rate-limited by the framework (see `AuthConfig.rateLimit`).

id.description: Provider id (the `[provider]` route segment): `"email"` / `"email-otp"` by default.

name.description: Display name for a sign-in button — `GET {basePath}/providers` echoes it.

type.description: Discriminant marking this as an email provider.

mode.description: `"magic"` mails a link (opened on a confirmation page whose button redeems it, unless `confirm: false`); `"otp"` mails a code (redeemed by a POST).

allowSignUp.description: Whether an address with no account may sign up by proving its mailbox. With `false` an unknown address is sent nothing — and answered exactly as if it had been.

confirm.description: `magicLink()` (unless `confirm: false`): the link's GET renders a confirmation page whose form POSTs the token, instead of spending it — so a mail gateway that pre-fetches links can't burn one, and nobody is signed in without pressing the button. Absent for `emailOtp()`; only an explicit `false` (`magicLink({ confirm: false })`) redeems on the GET.

id.description: Provider id (the `[provider]` route segment): `"phone"` by default.

name.description: Display name for a sign-in button — `GET {basePath}/providers` echoes it.

type.description: Discriminant marking this as a phone provider.

allowSignUp.description: Whether a number with no account may sign up by proving it. With `false` an unknown number is sent nothing — and answered exactly as if it had been.

name.description: Display name for a sign-in button.

metadataXml.description: The IdP's metadata XML (entity id, SSO URL, signing certificates).

domains.description: The email domains this IdP speaks for. An asserted address on one of them becomes the account's verified email; any other address is never bound to an account (the user signs in with no email). Without domains, no email is bound.

attributeMapping.description: Map the assertion's attributes to user metadata (`{ email: "mail", name: "displayName" }`); the email defaults to the NameID when it is an address, else to `email` / `mail`.

linkExistingAccounts.description: Link a first sign-in to an EXISTING account with the same email address when the address is on one of domains (default `false`: such a sign-in is refused, `?error=account_not_linked`). Turn it on only for an IdP you trust to speak for every address in its domains.

allowSignUp.description: Create a new user on a first sign-in (default `true`).

sp.description: This service provider's entity id and keys (see SamlProviderSp).

signingKey.description: Signs AuthnRequests (RSA-SHA256): a PKCS #8 PEM or an RSA private JWK.

signingCertificate.description: The X.509 certificate (PEM) of signingKey, published in the SP metadata.

encryptionKey.description: Decrypts encrypted assertions (RSA-OAEP): a PKCS #8 PEM or an RSA private JWK.

encryptionCertificate.description: The X.509 certificate (PEM) of encryptionKey, published `use="encryption"`.

secret.description: HMAC signing secret(s) for the session cookie (rotate with an array). At least 32 chars: shorter warns in development and makes `denextAuth()` throw in production.

canonicalOrigin.description: The app's canonical origin (e.g. `https://example.com`). REQUIRED in production so the OAuth `redirect_uri` is byte-stable and immune to Host-header injection.

trustForwardedHeaders.description: The app runs behind a proxy/load balancer that sets `x-forwarded-for`, so every per-IP rate-limit budget (and `signInFailed`'s `ip`) may key on that header's LAST hop (the one the proxy appended). Off by default — without a proxy the header is attacker-controlled, and the limiters key on the socket peer instead. **Unset, it inherits the app-level `trustForwardedHeaders` / `DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`**, so the auth limiters and `clientIp()` agree on the client; set it only to override the app for auth.

signIn.description: Return false to deny a sign-in, or a modified user to enrich the session.

session.description: Adjust the session payload before it is issued.

authorized.description: The authorization hook `requireAuth` consults once a live session exists — richer than `role`, because it sees the request. Return `true` to allow, `false` to refuse exactly as an unauthenticated request is refused (a redirect to the sign-in page carrying `callbackUrl`), or your own `Response` (a 403 page, a JSON envelope) to have it returned verbatim.

pages.description: Where to send the user after sign-in / sign-out when no `callbackUrl` is given.

signIn.description: The sign-in page (default `/`) — also where a refused guard redirects.

mfa.description: Where a session that still owes a second factor is sent (default: `signIn`).

verifyRequest.description: The "check your email" page shown after a verification token is sent.

error.description: A page that renders `?error=` codes for the emailed flows (a bad verification, reset, sign-in link or code) instead of the sign-in page. OAuth callback and guard errors still land on `signIn`.

dangerouslyAllowInsecureProviders.description: DANGEROUS: permit `http://localhost` providers in development (bypasses the SSRF localhost block for token/userinfo/jwks). Never enable in production.

rateLimit.description: Brute-force protection. ON by default, with five budgets that each answer a generic `429`: credentials, 5 failed attempts per client IP + identifier per 15 minutes; sign-in starts (`/signin/*`), 100 per client IP per 15 minutes (`rateLimit.signin`); session reads (`GET /session`), 300 per client IP per minute (`rateLimit.session`); emailed tokens (verification, reset, magic link, one-time code), 3 sends per address per 15 minutes (`rateLimit.verification`); second factors, 5 attempts per user per 5 minutes (`rateLimit.mfa`). Tune the limits, key, or store here, or pass `false` to disable every limiter (e.g. you rate-limit at the edge). The default store is per-process — pass a shared `store` for multi-replica deployments.

max.description: Failed attempts allowed per key per window before a `429`. Default 5.

windowMs.description: Window length in ms. Default 15 minutes.

keyGenerator.description: Derive the limiter key from the request + the submitted credentials. The default combines the client IP (the socket peer; behind a proxy declared with `AuthConfig.trustForwardedHeaders`, the last `x-forwarded-for` hop) with the submitted identifier (`email` / `username` / `login` / `identifier`, lower-cased). Override when your proxy uses another header or you want a coarser/finer key.

store.description: A shared store (Redis, SQL, …) instead of the per-process in-memory default.

signin.description: Tune the **sign-in-start** limiter — the per-IP budget for `GET {basePath}/signin/:provider`, which is counted on every hit rather than only on failures. `max`/`windowMs`/`keyGenerator` above belong to the credentials limiter and never apply here; `store` is shared by both (their keys are namespaced apart).

max.description: Sign-in starts allowed per client IP per window before a `429`. Default 100.

windowMs.description: Window length in ms. Default 15 minutes.

session.description: Tune the **session-read** limiter — the per-IP budget for `GET {basePath}/session`, counted on every hit. Default 300 per minute, which is far above any sane `SessionProvider` poll and still bounds an unauthenticated flood. Like `signin`, it shares `store` and ignores `max`/`windowMs`/`keyGenerator`.

max.description: Session reads allowed per client IP per window before a `429`. Default 300.

windowMs.description: Window length in ms. Default 1 minute.

verification.description: Tune the **verification** limiter — outbound-token requests (password-reset, email-verification, magic-link and one-time-code sends), counted on every request for an address whether or not the address has an account, so a throttled unknown address answers exactly like a throttled known one. The IP-wide bucket allows `IP_BUCKET_FACTOR` (10)× `max`. Shares `store`; ignores the credentials `max`/`windowMs`/`keyGenerator`.

max.description: Requests allowed per address per window before a `429`. Default 3.

windowMs.description: Window length in ms. Default 15 minutes.

mfa.description: Tune the **MFA** limiter — second-factor attempts per user, plus an IP-wide bucket at `IP_BUCKET_FACTOR` (10)× `max`. Shares `store`; ignores the credentials fields.

max.description: Attempts allowed per user per window before a `429`. Default 5.

windowMs.description: Window length in ms. Default 5 minutes.

captcha.description: Tune the **captcha** limiter — the per-IP budget spent on every captcha token denext is about to send to the provider (denext's own endpoints and `/auth/v1` alike), BEFORE the provider is called, so no unauthenticated request stream can drive unlimited verifier calls. A missing or oversized token is refused without spending. `false` turns this one budget off. Shares `store`; ignores the credentials fields. Skipped, like every per-IP budget, for a loopback/private peer with no trusted proxy hop.

max.description: Verifier calls allowed per client IP per window before a `429`. Default 30.

windowMs.description: Window length in ms. Default 1 minute.

sessionStore.description: Opt in to **server-side, revocable sessions**. When set, the cookie carries only a random session id and the payload lives in the store, so `revokeSession` / `revokeAllSessions` end sessions immediately (a stolen cookie, a password change). When unset (the default) sessions are stateless signed cookies — zero-config and multi-replica-safe, but only expiry can end them. See `inMemorySessionStore` / `sqliteSessionStore`, and note a per-process store isn't shared across replicas.

adapter.description: Where users, linked accounts, credentials, verification tokens, API tokens and MFA factors are persisted. Optional: without one, denext stays the stateless OAuth/Credentials layer it has always been and `session.user.id` is whatever the provider's `profile` mapper returned. **With** one, sign-in resolves (or creates) an adapter user and `session.user.id` becomes that adapter id. An adapter does **not** make sessions stateful — see AuthSessionConfig.strategy.

getUser.description: Look a user up by id.

getUserByEmail.description: Look a user up by email (case-insensitively, if the store can).

getUserByAccount.description: Look a user up by a linked provider account — the primary sign-in path.

updateUser.description: Merge changed fields into a user.

getUserByPhone.description: Look a user up by phone number (optional; gates phone sign-in). Numbers are stored and matched in E.164 form.

listUsers.description: One page of users, oldest first (optional; gates the admin user listing).

linkAccount.description: Link a provider account to a user.

listAccounts.description: Every provider account linked to a user (optional).

useVerificationToken.description: **Atomically** redeem a verification token: delete it and return what it was, or return `undefined` when it is absent (already spent, or never existed). The delete and the read MUST happen as one operation — two concurrent redemptions of the same token must produce exactly one record. An expired token is consumed too but resolves `undefined` (fail closed) — it is never left to be retried.

getCredential.description: The stored password hash for a user (optional).

setCredential.description: Set (or replace) a user's password hash (optional).

deleteCredential.description: Remove a user's password hash (optional). A pre-account-hijacking eviction uses it to retire a password set before the address was proven; without it the hash is overwritten with one of a random secret instead. Removing a password the user doesn't have is not an error.

getApiTokenByHash.description: Look a bearer token up by the hash of the presented string (optional).

touchApiToken.description: Record a successful presentation (optional; best-effort, never fails a request).

listApiTokens.description: A user's bearer tokens (optional). Implementations never return the secret.

setMfa.description: Store (or replace) a user's TOTP factor (optional).

deleteMfa.description: Remove a user's TOTP factor and backup codes (optional). `disableTotp` and the pre-account-hijacking eviction use it; without it they write an empty, unconfirmed record, which reads as "not enrolled" everywhere. Removing a factor the user doesn't have is not an error.

replaceMfaSecret.description: **Atomically** replace a user's stored TOTP secret, only while it still equals `expected` (optional) — how a pre-4.0 record's secret is cleared once it has moved into a factor. A compare-and-swap of that one field, never a whole-record write: a concurrent `consumeBackupCode` must not be undone. Without it the move falls back to `setMfa`.

consumeBackupCode.description: **Atomically** spend one backup code. Backup codes are stored salted-and-hashed, so the adapter cannot look one up by value: it walks MfaRecord.backupCodeHashes, `await`s `matches(hash)` for each, and — still inside the same transaction / critical section — removes the first hash that matches and reports `true`. Two concurrent redemptions of the same code must yield exactly one `true`.

claimTotpStep.description: **Atomically** claim a TOTP time step, the replay guard for a valid code presented twice. Succeeds only when `step` is strictly greater than the stored MfaRecord.lastStep, and stores it in the same operation. Two concurrent presentations of one code must yield exactly one `true`.

createMfaFactor.description: Store a new factor (optional; the factor group gates `/auth/v1/factors`).

updateMfaFactor.description: Change a factor's status, label, secret (a re-sealed TOTP secret, a WebAuthn factor's credential id) or challenge time.

claimMfaFactorStep.description: **Atomically** claim a TOTP step on a factor: succeeds only when `step` is greater than its stored `lastStep`, and stores it in the same operation (the replay guard).

deleteMfaFactor.description: Remove a factor. Removing an unknown one is not an error.

createNativeGrant.description: Store a single-use native grant (a code or a nonce) — hash only (optional; the native session group gates `denextAuth({ native })`).

useNativeGrant.description: **Atomically** redeem a native grant: delete it and return what it was, or `undefined` when absent. Two concurrent redemptions must produce exactly one record. An expired grant is consumed too but resolves `undefined` (fail closed).

createNativeSession.description: Store a new native session family.

getNativeSession.description: A native session family by id, exactly as stored (revoked and expired ones included — the caller decides; reuse detection needs to see a revoked family).

rotateNativeSession.description: **Atomically** advance a family from `fromGeneration` to `fromGeneration + 1` — a compare-and-swap that succeeds only while the stored generation is still `fromGeneration` and the family is not revoked. Two concurrent refreshes with one token yield exactly one `true`. The same write stores `rotation.rotatedAt` as NativeSessionRecord.rotatedAt.

revokeNativeSession.description: Revoke one family (sign-out, or refresh-token reuse). Revoking an unknown or already revoked family is a no-op.

revokeNativeSessionsByUser.description: Revoke every family of a user ("sign out everywhere", password reset) — except `exceptId`, when given ("sign out my other sessions").

createPasskey.description: Store a newly registered passkey (optional; the passkey group gates `denextAuth({ passkeys })`). **Atomic** against a duplicate ID: when a credential with this `id` is already registered — to anyone — store nothing and return `false` (WebAuthn L3 §7.1 step 25).

updatePasskey.description: **Atomically** record a verified assertion: a compare-and-swap that writes `update` only while the stored `signCount` is still `fromSignCount`, so two assertions racing on one counter value can't both pass the clone check.

deletePasskey.description: Remove a passkey. Removing an unknown one is not an error.

usePasskeyChallenge.description: **Atomically** redeem a challenge: delete it and return what it was, or `undefined` when absent. Two concurrent redemptions must produce exactly one record; an expired one is consumed too but resolves `undefined`.

createSsoProvider.description: Store a new SSO provider and its domains, **atomically** refusing a duplicate entity id or a domain another provider holds (optional; the group gates `/auth/v1/admin/sso/providers`).

updateSsoProvider.description: Replace a stored provider (and its domains) by id, with the same uniqueness rules.

getSsoProviderByEntityId.description: The provider with this entity id.

getSsoProviderByDomain.description: The provider a domain routes to.

deleteSsoProvider.description: Remove a provider, its domains and its SSO session records.

createSsoSession.description: Record the SSO origin of a session family (and drop expired records).

listSsoSessions.description: The unexpired session records of one NameID at one provider.

claimSamlMessageId.description: **Atomically** claim a SAML message id (an assertion or logout message ID, namespaced by the caller): `true` the first time, `false` for every later claim while it is kept. Kept at least until `expiresAt` (epoch seconds) — the replay cache every replica shares.

recordSsoSessionIndex.description: Record that a SAML sign-in at `providerId` started the cookie session `sid` (and prune expired index rows).

listSsoSessionIndexBySessionIndex.description: The unexpired cookie sessions one SessionIndex of a NameID started.

listSsoSessionIndexByNameId.description: The unexpired cookie sessions a NameID started, every SessionIndex.

revokeSids.description: Put cookie sessions on the revocation list until `expiresAt` (and prune expired entries). Never evicted early.

isSidRevoked.description: Whether the cookie session `sid` is on the revocation list (and not expired).

deleteUser.description: Delete a user and everything keyed by them: linked accounts, the password hash, bearer API tokens, the MFA factor, native session families, and verification tokens issued to their address (optional; gates `POST {basePath}/account/delete`). Deleting an unknown user is not an error.

sessions.description: An optional SessionStore over the same storage. It is used only when the app asks for `session: { strategy: "database" }` (or passes `sessionStore` itself) — an adapter never silently makes sessions stateful.

rateLimits.description: An optional RateLimitStore over the same storage. The auth limiters use it when the app runs on `@denext/backend`'s Postgres and sets no `rateLimit.store`, so every replica counts against one budget.

close.description: Optional: release resources (a database handle) when the server drains.

session.description: Session lifetime, sliding refresh, and cookie-vs-database storage.

strategy.description: `"cookie"` (default) keeps the whole payload in the signed cookie — stateless, multi-replica-safe, only expiry ends it. `"database"` stores the payload server-side and puts only a random id in the cookie, so sessions are revocable; it requires a store — either AuthConfig.sessionStore or an adapter that exposes `sessions` — and throws at config time when neither is present.

maxAge.description: Session lifetime in seconds (default 7 days). Overrides the legacy top-level `maxAge`.

updateAge.description: Refresh a session's expiry when it is older than this many seconds — "sliding" sessions. `0` (the default) never refreshes. Only endpoints that own the `Response` can set a cookie, so the refresh happens on `GET {basePath}/session`, `requireAuth`, `requireSession` and `updateAuthSession()` — never inside a bare `auth()`.

maxLifetime.description: The absolute session lifetime in seconds: a hard ceiling counted from the sign-in (`authTime`) that sliding refresh never extends. A session is refused once it is this old, whatever its `expiresAt` says, on both strategies; a step-up to a second factor is a new authentication and starts a new ceiling. Default: 30 days, or `maxAge` when that is longer, so a session that never slides is unaffected. Must be a whole number of seconds no shorter than `maxAge` (`denextAuth()` throws otherwise). Native app sessions have their own cap, `native.refreshTokenMaxAge`.

basePath.description: Mount the endpoints under this prefix instead of `/auth` (e.g. `"/account/auth"`). A leading slash is added and a trailing one stripped; `"/"` is refused, because the handler would then claim every request.

cookies.description: Override the session / OAuth-transaction cookie names and attributes.

name.description: The cookie name *before* the `__Host-` prefix. Defaults are `"denext_auth"` (session) and `"denext_auth_tx"` (OAuth transaction) — changing one logs every existing session of that kind out once.

hostPrefix.description: Origin-lock the cookie with the `__Host-` name prefix (Secure + `Path=/` + no `Domain`). **On by default**, and leaving it on is strongly recommended: it is what stops a sibling subdomain reading or shadowing the cookie. Over plain http on a loopback host, or outside production, the prefix is left off for that request (a browser refuses `__Host-` over http, even on `localhost`).

sameSite.description: Cookie `SameSite` (default `"Lax"` — the OAuth callback is a top-level GET).

name.description: The cookie name *before* the `__Host-` prefix. Defaults are `"denext_auth"` (session) and `"denext_auth_tx"` (OAuth transaction) — changing one logs every existing session of that kind out once.

hostPrefix.description: Origin-lock the cookie with the `__Host-` name prefix (Secure + `Path=/` + no `Domain`). **On by default**, and leaving it on is strongly recommended: it is what stops a sibling subdomain reading or shadowing the cookie. Over plain http on a loopback host, or outside production, the prefix is left off for that request (a browser refuses `__Host-` over http, even on `localhost`).

sameSite.description: Cookie `SameSite` (default `"Lax"` — the OAuth callback is a top-level GET).

events.description: Lifecycle hooks (sign-in, sign-out, failures, revocation, user/account creation).

signInFailed.description: A sign-in attempt was refused (bad credentials, a denied callback, a bad state).

apiTokenIssued.description: A bearer API token was minted (`issueApiToken`, `POST {basePath}/tokens`). Never carries the token or its hash.

apiTokenRevoked.description: A bearer API token was revoked: by `revokeApiToken` / `DELETE {basePath}/tokens/:id` (`"revoked"`), by a password reset (`"password_reset"`), or by the first proof of an unverified account's mailbox (`"email_verified"`) or phone number (`"phone_verified"`) — the pre-account-hijacking eviction.

sessionRevoked.description: A server-side session was revoked (one device, or everywhere).

createUser.description: An adapter user record was created.

linkAccount.description: A provider account was linked to an existing user.

verificationRequested.description: A verification token was delivered through `sendVerificationRequest` / `hooks.sendEmail` (an email-verification or password-reset email, or a `magicLink()` / `emailOtp()` sign-in link or code), or a `phoneOtp()` code through the SMS sender (`purpose: "sms"`, the number as `identifier`). Fires only for a real send — never for an unknown address, a throttled request or a failed delivery — and never carries the token or the link.

emailVerified.description: A user proved control of their address: by redeeming an email-verification token, or by a first magic-link / one-time-code sign-in into an existing unverified account — whose password, bearer tokens and server-side sessions were retired first (`sessionRevoked` fired for the sessions).

phoneVerified.description: A user proved control of their phone number by a first `phoneOtp()` sign-in into an existing account whose number was unverified — whose password, second factors, passkeys, bearer tokens and server-side sessions were retired first (`sessionRevoked` fired for the sessions).

userConverted.description: An anonymous user became permanent: a complete anonymous session redeemed an email link / code or a phone code for an identifier no account had, so the proof was attached to the anonymous user (same id, `isAnonymous` cleared) instead of creating a new one.

passwordReset.description: A user set a new password by redeeming a password-reset token. Their server-side sessions have already been revoked when this fires (`sessionRevoked` fired too).

logger.description: Where the framework logs. Silent by default — auth never writes to the console.

error.description: A swallowed failure — a provider round-trip, an adapter write, an event handler.

hasher.description: How user-supplied secrets (Credentials passwords, MFA backup codes) are hashed and checked. Defaults to `scryptHasher()`.

hash.description: Hash a plaintext secret for storage.

verify.description: Check a plaintext secret against a stored hash.

sendVerificationRequest.description: Deliver a verification token (email verification, password reset, magic link, OTP). `smtpMailer({ host, user, pass, from })` sends them over SMTP (TLS required); the flows that need one refuse to start without this (or `hooks.sendEmail`).

sendSms.description: Deliver an SMS — phone sign-in codes (`phoneOtp()`), phone MFA codes and phone changes, for denext's own endpoints and for `/auth/v1` (`backend({ supabase })`) alike. denext ships no SMS gateway; the phone flows refuse to start without this (or `hooks.sendSms`).

captcha.description: Verify a captcha token (hCaptcha or Turnstile) on the endpoints that create sessions or send messages — sign-up, password sign-in, one-time codes, recovery, anonymous sign-in — on denext's endpoints and `/auth/v1` alike. Off by default. denext's endpoints (the credentials POST, an email or phone SEND, `POST /anonymous`, `POST /reset`) read the token from `captchaToken`, `captcha_token`, `cf-turnstile-response` or `h-captcha-response` in the body, or the `x-captcha-token` header, and refuse without one the provider confirms (`400 { error: "captcha_failed" }`, or a form's `303 ?error=CaptchaFailed`) before any adapter work or rate-limit spend. Redeeming a code or link needs no token.

hooks.description: Supabase's auth hooks, shared by denext's endpoints and `/auth/v1`: `customAccessToken` shapes the claims of every session (an `/auth/v1` access token, and the `request.jwt.claims` a cookie session's queries run with), `sendEmail` delivers every auth email (instead of `sendVerificationRequest`), `sendSms` every SMS (instead of `sendSms`).

customAccessToken.description: Shape every access token: return the claims to sign (Supabase's Custom Access Token Hook). `sub`, `role`, `aud`, `session_id`, `iat`, `exp`, `aal` and `is_anonymous` are restored after it runs (it may add claims and change `app_metadata` / `user_metadata` / `email` / `phone` in the token only). A throw refuses the sign-in.

sendEmail.description: Deliver every auth email yourself (replaces `sendVerificationRequest` for `/auth/v1`).

sendSms.description: Deliver every auth SMS yourself (replaces GoTrueOptions.sendSms).

anonymous.description: Anonymous sign-in: a user with no identifier yet (`POST {basePath}/anonymous`, `supabase.auth.signInAnonymously()`), who becomes permanent by adding a confirmed email or phone — on denext's endpoints by redeeming an email link / code or a `phoneOtp()` code for an identifier no account has, from the anonymous session. Default `false`: the endpoint does not exist.

email.description: Token lifetimes and link targets for email verification, password reset, magic links and one-time codes.

verifyMaxAge.description: How long an email-verification link stays valid, in seconds. Default `86400` (24 hours).

resetMaxAge.description: How long a password-reset link stays valid, in seconds. Default `3600` (1 hour).

magicMaxAge.description: How long a magic sign-in link stays valid, in seconds. Default `600` (10 minutes).

otpMaxAge.description: How long a one-time code stays valid, in seconds — an emailed one and a `phoneOtp()` text alike. Default `300` (5 minutes).

otpDigits.description: How many digits a one-time code (email or SMS) has. Default `6`; clamped to `6..10`.

verifyPath.description: The same-origin path an email-verification link opens (the link adds `?token=…&email=…`). Default `{basePath}/verify` — `"/auth/verify"` — the built-in endpoint, which verifies the address and redirects. Must start with a single `/`.

resetPath.description: The same-origin path a password-reset link opens (the link adds `?token=…&email=…`) — a page YOUR app renders: a form posting `email`, `token` and the new `password` to `{basePath}/reset/confirm`. Default `{basePath}/reset` — `"/auth/reset"`; the auth endpoints only claim a POST there, so a GET falls through to e.g. `app/auth/reset/page.tsx`. Must start with a single `/`.

required.description: Who must present a second factor: `"enrolled"` (the default) asks only users who have enrolled one; `"always"` asks everyone, sending a user without a factor to enrol first. Any other value reads as `"enrolled"`.

issuer.description: The issuer label an authenticator app shows next to the account. Default: the host name of `canonicalOrigin`, else `"denext"`.

window.description: How many 30-second TOTP steps of clock drift are accepted either side of now. Default `1` (±30 seconds); clamped to `0..2`.

backupCodes.description: How many single-use backup codes enrollment mints. Default `10`; clamped to `0..20`.

freshness.description: How recent, in seconds, a second-factor proof must be for an action that demands a fresh one (step-up). Default `900` (15 minutes); clamped to `0..31536000`. `0` means such an action always asks for a code.

passkeys.description: Passkeys (WebAuthn): `POST {basePath}/passkey/*` registers them from a signed-in session and signs in with them (a first factor, or the second factor of a pending session). Needs an adapter with the passkey group (both shipped adapters have it). `true` takes every default. See AuthPasskeyConfig.

rpId.description: The relying party ID credentials are scoped to: the host of `canonicalOrigin` by default, or a registrable suffix of it (`"example.com"` for `https://app.example.com`) to share passkeys across subdomains. Every accepted origin's host must equal it or end in `.<rpId>` (WebAuthn L3 §5.1.4.1).

rpName.description: The relying party name an authenticator may show. Default: the RP ID.

origins.description: The origins a ceremony may come from, matched exactly against `clientDataJSON.origin`. Default: `[canonicalOrigin]`. Add a second web origin here; an Android app goes in androidApps (an `android:apk-key-hash:<43 base64url characters>` entry here is accepted too, checked for that exact form).

androidApps.description: Android apps whose passkey ceremonies are accepted: inside an app, Credential Manager reports `clientDataJSON.origin` as `android:apk-key-hash:<base64url SHA-256 of the signing certificate>`, and each listed fingerprint adds that exact origin to origins. The app calls `/native/passkey/*` (with `native` sessions configured) or, from a page on this origin, the cookie rows. Android also requires the domain's `assetlinks.json` to delegate `get_login_creds` to the app: pass the same objects to `appLinks.android` in `denext.config.ts`. With Play App Signing, list Play's app signing key (Play Console → Test and release → App integrity) and the upload / debug keys you test with (`keytool -list -v -keystore <keystore>`).

sha256CertFingerprints.description: The SHA-256 fingerprints of the certificates the app is signed with: `AB:CD:…` (32 colon-separated hex pairs, as `keytool` and the Play Console print them) or 64 hex digits.

corsOrigins.description: The web origins allowed to call the passkey endpoints from another origin — a front end served apart from the auth server (`["https://www.example.com"]` for an auth server at `https://auth.example.com`). Each must also be in origins (its page runs the ceremony). The endpoints then answer their preflights and send credentialed CORS headers to exactly these origins, and a ceremony started from one completes only from that origin, with client data naming it — on top of the per-tab ceremony id. Default: none (same-origin only). Pass `origin` to the `denext/client` passkey calls on that front end.

userVerification.description: `"required"` (the default) asks the authenticator to verify the user (biometric, PIN) and refuses an assertion without the UV flag — such a sign-in is two factors in one, so it also satisfies a pending second factor. `"preferred"` accepts a presence-only assertion, which is one factor: a user with TOTP is then still asked for a code.

timeout.description: How long a ceremony's challenge lives, in seconds. Default `300`; clamped to `30..900`.

attestation.description: Attestation policy for new passkeys. Off by default: any supported attestation (`none`, `packed`, `tpm`, `android-key`, `android-safetynet`, `apple`, `fido-u2f`, `compound`) registers once its statement verifies, and a certificate in it is not chained to anything (except `android-safetynet`'s, which must chain to Google's root).

mds.description: Check registrations against the FIDO Metadata Service (MDS3): the authenticator's certificate must chain to its model's metadata roots, and a model whose metadata reports a compromise is refused. Registration options then ask for `attestation: "direct"`. See AuthPasskeyMdsConfig.

url.description: The BLOB's URL (`https:` only). Default: `https://mds.fidoalliance.org/`. A mirror works: the BLOB is verified against the pinned FIDO root wherever it came from.

blob.description: The BLOB itself (the JWT text), or a function returning it — for a server without outbound network. Verified exactly like a fetched one; when set, `url` is never fetched.

revocation.description: What a revocation status that can't be had (no usable OCSP answer, no usable CRL) means, for a certificate of the BLOB's or an attestation's path that names an OCSP responder or CRL distribution points: `"require"` refuses the path (fail closed), `"best-effort"` goes on without it (a certificate reported revoked is still refused), `"off"` asks nothing. Default: `passkeys.attestation.revocation` (`"hard"` is `"require"`, `"soft"` is `"best-effort"`); with neither, `"require"`, or `"best-effort"` when blob supplies the BLOB.

maxBytes.description: The largest BLOB accepted, bytes. Default 32 MiB.

allowUnattested.description: Accept `none` and self attestation (no certificate, so no model is proven), still refusing an AAGUID whose metadata reports compromise. Default `false`: only an attestation that chains to its authenticator's metadata roots registers. Synced passkeys attest `none`, so turn this on unless every user has a certified security key.

allowUnknownAuthenticators.description: Accept a certificate attestation whose AAGUID has no metadata entry (its chain is then not checked). Default `false`.

revocation.description: What an unreachable revocation source means for a certificate of a path mds validates (the BLOB's signing chain, an attestation's `x5c` chain) that names an OCSP responder or a CRL distribution point. `"hard"` refuses the path (fail closed); `"soft"` goes on without a status, logging a warning. Default `"hard"`, or `"soft"` when `mds.blob` supplies the BLOB (a server without outbound network). A certificate a usable OCSP answer or CRL reports revoked is refused under both. `mds.revocation`, when set, takes precedence.

native.description: Native session mode for a Capacitor (or desktop) app: code exchange → bearer access token + rotating refresh token, and native Apple / Google `id_token` sign-in. See AuthNativeConfig.

redirectUris.description: The app callback URIs a code may be delivered to, matched EXACTLY (e.g. `"com.example.app://auth/callback"`, or a claimed `https://` universal link). A loopback `http://127.0.0.1/…` / `http://[::1]/…` entry matches any port (RFC 8252 §7.3), for a desktop app's ephemeral listener. Plain `http:` elsewhere, `javascript:`, `data:` and `file:` are refused.

accessTokenTtl.description: Access-token lifetime in seconds (default 900; clamped to 60..3600).

refreshTokenTtl.description: How long a refresh token stays usable, in seconds; each refresh slides it forward (default 30 days; clamped to 1 hour..1 year).

refreshTokenMaxAge.description: An absolute cap on a session family, in seconds from its original sign-in: however often the app refreshes, the family stops refreshing (and is revoked) this long after the user signed in, and they sign in again. Default: none — a family used within every `refreshTokenTtl` lives indefinitely. Clamped to 1 hour..10 years.

refreshReuseInterval.description: A grace window, in seconds, for two refreshes racing with one refresh token (a background task and the foreground app, two processes). Within this long after a rotation, presenting the IMMEDIATELY previous refresh token answers the same token pair that rotation issued, instead of treating it as a replay and revoking the family. An older generation, or the previous one after the window, is still a replay. Default `10`, as GoTrue's `GOTRUE_SECURITY_REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSE_INTERVAL`; `0` is strict (any reuse revokes); clamped to 0..60. Inside the window a replayed previous token gets the pair its legitimate use got — set `0` where that matters more than a refresh race.

codeTtl.description: One-time code lifetime in seconds (default 60; clamped to 10..600).

requireNonce.description: Require a server-issued nonce (`POST {basePath}/native/nonce`) in every native id_token sign-in (default `true`), so a captured id_token can't be replayed.

clientSecret.description: The client-secret JWT (ES256, signed with your Apple key, at most 6 months) — or a function returning a fresh one. With it, a native sign-in that passes Apple's `authorizationCode` stores the Apple refresh token, and account deletion revokes it at `https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke` (App Store guideline 5.1.1(v)). Without it (and without an `apple()` web provider to borrow it from) nothing is revoked, and deletion says so to the logger.

clientIds.description: The client ids an `id_token` may be issued to — every one the app signs in with (Apple: the iOS bundle id and, for the web, the Services ID; Google: the iOS client id and the web client id Android's Credential Manager uses as `serverClientId`). The token's `aud` must be one of them, and a multi-valued `aud` or any `azp` must name one of them too.

allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking.description: DANGEROUS, as on an OAuth provider: link to an existing local account whose address is unverified. Off by default.

issuers.description: Advanced (tests, a private issuer): the accepted `iss` values.

jwksUrl.description: Advanced (tests, a private issuer): the JWKS URL.

fetch.description: Test / advanced seam: the fetch used for the providers' JWKS and Apple's token and revoke endpoints. Default: `safeFetch`, pinned to the provider's hosts.

onAccountDeleted.description: Called after `POST {basePath}/account/delete` removed a user (and revoked their sessions and Apple tokens) — delete the app's own rows for them here. Awaited; a throw is logged, never shown to the caller (the account is already gone).

plugins.name: @denext/avif
plugins.title: @denext/avif
plugins.blurb: A Deno-native AVIF encoder and decoder — denext's first-party, zero-npm replacement for the @jsquash/avif peer codec its image optimizer used to lazily import.

plugins.name: @denext/backend
plugins.title: @denext/backend
plugins.blurb: Backend services inside your denext app, as one opt-in plugin: no hosted service, nothing to run beside it.

storage.description: File storage: a driver and the buckets it serves.

location.description: Where the store is, for a store reached over the network: its endpoint's origin (`https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`). Absent for one on this machine's disk (fs).

init.description: Called once at plugin setup with the project root (resolve relative paths against it).

put.description: Store an object. The stream errors when the body breaks a rule; the driver then stores nothing.

get.description: Read an object (a range of it), or `null` when it does not exist.

head.description: An object's info, or `null` when it does not exist.

remove.description: Delete an object (no error when it does not exist).

list.description: One page of the objects whose key starts with `prefix`, in key order.

direct.description: Direct-to-store URLs, when the store serves clients itself (S3).

presignGet.description: A presigned GET. `disposition` and `contentType`, when given, are signed in as the store's `response-content-disposition` / `response-content-type` overrides, so the store serves the object with them (a store without such overrides must refuse rather than drop them).

createMultipart.description: Start a multipart upload; returns its upload id.

presignPart.description: A presigned PUT for one part (1-based). With `size`, the part's `content-length` is signed too, so the store itself refuses a part of any other size.

completeMultipart.description: Assemble the uploaded parts into the object.

abortMultipart.description: Abandon a multipart upload and free its parts.

uploadPart.description: Upload one part from the server (resumable uploads); returns its ETag. Optional: without it, the part is sent to presignPart's URL.

copy.description: Copy an object inside the store (S3 `CopyObject`), keeping its content type. Optional: without it, a copy streams the object back in through `get` and `put`.

buckets.description: The buckets, by name (lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`).

public.description: Anyone may download (no signature, no authorize call), and download URLs are stable and cacheable. Uploads, deletes and listings still need authorize. Default `false`.

maxBytes.description: Largest object accepted, in bytes (default 50 MiB).

mime.description: Allowed content types — exact (`application/pdf`) or `type/*` (`image/*`). Checked on every upload; a declared raster image is also sniffed from its first bytes and must be what it claims. Omitted: any type.

authorize.description: Decide one operation for the current request. Runs whenever a storage call is made inside a request (the plugin's endpoints, and the server API called from a route handler, Server Action or page); a call outside any request (a job, a script) is trusted and skips it. Absent, every operation is denied — except downloads from a public bucket.

versioned.description: Object versioning, as Supabase Storage has it: `true` keeps every overwritten or deleted object as a noncurrent version (a delete leaves a delete marker); `false` suspends it (history is kept, new writes replace). Omitted: off (`DISABLED`), or whatever the bucket's row says once it has been turned on.

secret.description: The HMAC secret (≥ 32 characters) for the plugin's signed URLs and upload tokens — or a list, current first, to rotate one out. Default: `DENEXT_STORAGE_SECRET`; under `denext dev` a random per-process secret when neither is set.

multipartThreshold.description: Uploads larger than this go multipart, when the driver supports it (default 64 MiB).

partSize.description: Multipart part size in bytes (default 16 MiB, at least 5 MiB).

authorize.description: The rule for buckets created at runtime (`storage.createBucket`, supabase-js `createBucket`) and for declared buckets without an `authorize` of their own. Absent, those buckets are open only to the service role (and to downloads, when public).

rls.description: Authorize with SQL row-level security on `storage.objects` / `storage.buckets`, as Supabase does: every operation runs its statement as the request's role (`anon` / `authenticated`, `auth.uid()` in your policies), so the policies decide; a bucket's `authorize`, when it has one, must allow it too. Needs `postgres`. Default `false` (the TypeScript rules decide).

api.description: The Supabase-compatible Storage API (what `supabase.storage` from `@supabase/supabase-js` talks to, and TUS resumable uploads): served under `/storage/v1` by default; a path to move it, or `false` to turn it off.

metadataPath.description: Where the bucket and object metadata lives without Postgres: a `node:sqlite` file (default `.denext-storage.db` in the project root; in a `denext build --compile` binary, `storage.db` in its state directory, and a relative path resolves against its working directory). With `postgres`, it is the `storage` schema.

maxTransformDimension.description: The largest width or height the API's image render routes produce (default 2500).

postgres.description: Postgres: the app's database, as `db()` from `@denext/backend/server` (and denext auth's, with `adapter: backendAuthAdapter()`). `{}` reads `DATABASE_URL`.

url.description: A `postgres://` URL (default: `DATABASE_URL`), opened with `Deno.SQL` — the Postgres client built into denext's Deno runtime — and closed when the server drains.

sql.description: A client to use instead of `url`: any `SqlClient` (on stock Deno, `fromPostgresJs(postgres(url))` with the npm `postgres` package). It is never closed by the plugin.

directUrl.description: A direct `postgres://` URL to the same database (default: `DATABASE_DIRECT_URL`), for when `url` / `sql` is a pooler in transaction mode (PgBouncer, Supavisor). What needs a session of its own runs on it: realtime's LISTEN, its reserved connections (`revalidate.owner: "one"`, the logical source), webhook delivery's wake-up, the REST schema-reload listener, and every migration and its lock. Queries, `db()` included, keep using the pooled one.

rls.description: Row-level security: `db()` runs every query as `anon` or `authenticated` with the request's claims, so Supabase-style policies apply. The roles and `auth.*` functions are created by a migration on first use unless `migrate: false`.

migrate.description: Apply the `backend_rls_0001` migration (the `anon` / `authenticated` roles, their grant to the connecting role, and the `auth.*` functions) on the first scoped query (default `true`). `false` when a DBA applies rlsSetupSql instead.

claims.description: Extra claims for a signed-in user's `request.jwt.claims` (read in SQL with `auth.jwt() ->> 'tenant'`). Merged over denext's own; `sub`, `role` and `email` cannot be overridden.

realtime.description: Realtime from the database: tables whose inserts, updates and deletes reach `useTableChanges` subscribers (each re-read under that subscriber's row-level security) and `onTableChange` hooks. Needs `postgres`.

tables.description: The tables to send changes from, by name: `{ notes: { events: ["insert"], key: "id" } }`. Optional when the publication lists them.

events.description: The changes to send (default all four: `["insert", "update", "delete", "truncate"]`).

key.description: The key column a change is identified by (default `"id"`).

schema.description: The table's schema (default: the connection's search path).

old.description: What a change carries of the row as it was before an update or a delete (Supabase's `old` record): `"key"` (the default) — the key column only, which is what Supabase sends for a table under row-level security; `"full"` — the whole old row, carried in the notification, so only when it fits (about 7.5 KB of JSON; a larger one arrives without it, with `errors: ["Error 413: Payload Too Large"]`). The old row reaches only subscribers who could see the row before the change.

publication.description: Also send changes from the tables in this Postgres publication — Supabase's way to opt a table in (`alter publication supabase_realtime add table notes`), so Supabase migrations work unchanged. Default `"supabase_realtime"` (created, empty, if it does not exist); `false` reads only tables. A table there needs a one-column primary key; its old row is the key, or the whole row when it has `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` and no row-level security (as Supabase sends it). Re-read every 10 seconds, so a table added or dropped while the app runs follows.

source.description: Where changes come from. `"notify"` (the default): a trigger per table sends the key with `pg_notify`, which works everywhere but serializes committing transactions on the notification queue. `"logical"`: logical decoding — a temporary `pgoutput` replication slot per server instance, read over a reserved connection — no triggers, no NOTIFY, commit timestamps from the WAL. It needs `wal_level = logical`, a connecting role with the `REPLICATION` attribute and a client with `reserve()` (`Deno.SQL`, or postgres.js through `fromPostgresJs`).

pollMs.description: How often the slot is read when it was empty, in milliseconds (default 50).

maxChanges.description: Changes read per round trip (default 10 000); a full batch is followed at once.

revalidate.description: Also `revalidateTag("table:<name>")` once per burst of changes, so `<Live>`, `useLive`, `useApi({ tags })` and `defineSubscription({ tags })` watchers of that tag are pushed (default `false`). `true` is `{ owner: "every" }`.

owner.description: `"every"` (the default): each instance revalidates for every burst its own listener receives — right for an instance-local cache. `"one"`: one instance per database does, elected with a session-level Postgres advisory lock held on a reserved connection; when that connection closes (the instance stops or dies) the next instance to see a burst takes over. Use `"one"` only when the cache is shared by every instance (a Postgres cache store); it needs a client with `reserve()` (`Deno.SQL`, or postgres.js through `fromPostgresJs`), and without one every instance revalidates.

migrate.description: Install the triggers by migration (recorded in `backend_migrations`) the first time realtime is used (default `true`). `false` when a database administrator applies realtimeSetupSql instead.

maxSubscribers.description: Subscriptions held at once on one server instance (default 10 000). A subscription whose subscriber disconnected is kept for a reconnect only while there is room: at the cap the oldest such one is dropped, and only live subscriptions refuse a new one.

maxSubscriptionsPerIdentity.description: Subscriptions one identity may hold on one server instance (default 64): a signed-in user across all their connections, or the signed-out visitors at one client address (`clientIpForLimits()`: one Live connection when the address is unknown or an untrusted loopback/private peer — set `trustForwardedHeaders` behind a proxy). It also bounds the distinct filters (re-read groups) an identity adds to a burst. Server-side `tableChanges` subscriptions are not counted.

queryTimeoutMs.description: The `statement_timeout`, in milliseconds, of every re-read and subscribe-time query (transaction-local; default 5 000). A re-read that times out becomes a `resync` for its subscribers.

maxTrackedKeys.description: Keys tracked per subscription, so a delete reaches only subscribers who could see the row (default 10 000); see the docs for what happens past it.

socket.description: Serve Supabase Realtime's protocol — `/realtime/v1/websocket` (Phoenix channels: `postgres_changes`, broadcast, presence, private channels) and the REST broadcast `/realtime/v1/api/broadcast` — so `@supabase/supabase-js`'s `supabase.channel(…)` works against the app. On by default; `false` turns it off; an object sets its limits.

maxConnections.description: Sockets held at once on one server instance (default 10 000).

maxConnectionsPerAddress.description: Sockets from one client address (`clientIpForLimits()` — set `trustForwardedHeaders` behind a proxy; default 100).

maxChannelsPerConnection.description: Channels one socket may join (default 100, as Supabase).

maxEventsPerSecond.description: Messages a socket may send per second, heartbeats included (default 100).

maxPayloadBytes.description: The largest broadcast payload, and tracked presence state, in bytes (default 256 KiB).

replay.description: Replay what a `useTableChanges` subscriber missed while its connection was down (on by default): each server instance keeps a journal of the changes it received (keys only, as the triggers send them), and a subscription whose browser reconnects within `retentionSeconds` is sent the changes after the last one it was delivered — re-read as that subscriber, under the same row-level security and delete rules as live changes. A gap the journal no longer covers (older than the retention, past `maxChangesPerTable`, or across a lost database listener) is an explicit `resync`. `false` turns it off: a reconnect is then always a `resync`.

retentionSeconds.description: How long a disconnected subscription is kept for a reconnect, and how long the journal keeps a change, in seconds (default 60).

maxChangesPerTable.description: Changes the journal keeps per table (default 10 000): an older gap is a `resync`.

rest.description: Auto-REST: the schema's tables (those the `anon` / `authenticated` roles hold a privilege on) served PostgREST-style under `/rest/v1/<table>` — filters, ordering, paging, inserts, filtered updates and deletes — each statement run through `db()`, so row-level security scopes it to the request's user. Row types are generated into `.denext/rest.ts`. Needs `postgres`.

schema.description: The schema whose tables are served (default `"public"`); `schemas` lists several.

schemas.description: The schemas served, the default first (`Accept-Profile` / `Content-Profile` pick another, supabase-js's `schema("api")`). Overrides `schema`.

tables.description: The relations to serve, by name (`"notes"`, or `"api.notes"`), or `"*"` (the default) for every relation of the schemas that the `anon` or `authenticated` role holds a privilege on AND that enforces row-level security: a table with RLS enabled, or a view created `with (security_invoker = true)`. Tables with RLS off, ordinary (owner's-rights) views, materialized views and foreign tables are skipped — one startup warning lists them — unless named here: a list exposes exactly the named relations, whatever their RLS. A listed table those roles cannot reach gets no route either. Functions are served when either role may EXECUTE them.

maxRows.description: The most rows one read returns, whatever `limit` asks for (default 1000).

maxBodyBytes.description: The largest request body accepted, in bytes (default 1 MiB).

maxConcurrent.description: The most REST statements running at once, so the routes cannot take every connection of the pool the rest of the app shares (default: half the pool's `max` when the client reports it — `Deno.SQL` and postgres.js do — else 5). A request past it waits up to a second, then is answered 503 `PGRST003` with `Retry-After`.

exactCount.description: Who may ask for `Prefer: count=exact` on a read — a full count, as costly as reading every matching row: `"authenticated"` (the default; an anonymous request is refused with 400), `"all"`, or `"never"`. `count=planned` (the planner's estimate) is open to everyone.

explain.description: Answer `Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.plan` with the statement's execution plan (default `false`: a 406). Plans reveal table sizes and indexes; turn this on in development only.

aggregates.description: Allow aggregate functions in `select=` (`amount.sum()`, `count()`, … grouped by the other selected columns) — PostgREST's `db-aggregates-enabled` (default `false`: a 400). An aggregate reads every matching row whatever `limit` says, so a caller could make the database scan a whole table; turn it on when the tables are small or the statement timeout bounds the cost.

rateLimit.description: A request budget per client: a signed-in user by their user id, anyone else by their client address (`clientIpForLimits()`'s rule — skipped for an untrusted loopback/private peer), the secret key never. Past it a request is answered 429 `over_request_rate_limit` with `Retry-After`, before any statement runs. Default `{ max: 1200, windowMs: 60_000 }` — 20 requests a second on average, far above what a page of supabase-js calls needs — counted in `store`, else in the shared store `denextAuth({ rateLimit: { store } })` configures (Redis, Postgres, Deno KV), else per process; `false` turns it off.

max.description: Requests one client (a user, or an address when signed out) may make per window. Default 1200.

windowMs.description: The window, in milliseconds. Default 60 000 (one minute).

store.description: Where the counts live. Default: the routes' own bounded in-memory store, per process (10 000 clients; one over its budget is kept until its window ends). Pass a shared store (`redisRateLimitStore()`, `postgresRateLimitStore()`, `denoKvRateLimitStore()` from `denext/server`, with a `prefix` of its own) so every replica counts against one budget. The auth rate-limit store (`denextAuth({ rateLimit: { store } })`) is never used for these: each request would write to it, and its lockout rules are the sign-in limiters'.

openapi.description: Describe the routes in `@denext/openapi`'s document (default `true`): with that plugin installed, `/openapi.json` (and its docs page, `denext openapi emit`, and the clients generated from it) lists every relation and function of every schema in `schemas` that the `anon` and `authenticated` roles can use — what the secret key alone reaches is left out — with typed rows, PostgREST's filters and its error body. A route of another schema than the default takes the `Accept-Profile` / `Content-Profile` header that picks it; where two schemas share a name, the path describes the first in `schemas` order. `false` keeps them out.

supabase.description: The Supabase-compatible surface: `true` (keys from the environment) or the keys and the `/auth/v1` options (`auth`). Installs the API keys (publishable / secret, and the legacy JWT keys) and the JWT signing keys that `resolveIdentity()`, `db()` and `auth()` recognize, serves GoTrue's `/auth/v1` over the `denextAuth()` users (with the JWKS at `/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`), and adds `denext backend keys`.

auth.description: `/auth/v1` (GoTrue) options: the site URL and redirect allow-list, sign-up and confirmation policy, anonymous users, SMS delivery, captcha, hooks, MFA and SAML. The users themselves, the providers and the email delivery come from `denextAuth()`.

functions.description: Edge Functions: `functions/<name>.ts` (or `functions/<name>/index.ts`) served at `/functions/v1/<name>` — what supabase-js's `functions.invoke` calls — each in a Deno Worker of its own. A module that calls `Deno.serve(handler)` or default-exports a handler runs unchanged. Callers need a valid identity unless `verifyJwt: false`. `{}` serves the directory with the defaults.

dir.description: The directory holding the functions, relative to the project (default `"functions"`, or `"supabase/functions"` when only that exists). A function is `<dir>/<name>.ts` or `<dir>/<name>/index.ts`; entries starting with `_` or `.` (`_shared/`) are not functions.

basePath.description: Where the functions are served, app-relative (default `"/functions/v1"`).

verifyJwt.description: Require a valid caller for every function unless it says otherwise (default `true`).

timeoutMs.description: The longest one request may run, in milliseconds (default 150 000, Supabase's free tier).

maxBodyBytes.description: The largest request body passed to a function, in bytes (default 20 MiB).

env.description: Environment variables every function reads from `Deno.env`, over the process's own.

url.description: The URL functions read as `SUPABASE_URL` (the `SUPABASE_URL` env var wins). Default: the app's `canonicalOrigin` (or `DENEXT_CANONICAL_ORIGIN`) plus its `basePath`, else the address the server listens on as this machine reaches it (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) — never a request's `Host`, which a client chooses: a worker keeps its environment for life, beside the service key.

verifyJwt.description: Require a valid caller (a signed-in session, or — once the Supabase-compatible keys are configured — a valid access token or API key) before the function runs. Default: the directory's `verifyJwt` (itself `true`).

timeoutMs.description: The longest one request may run, in milliseconds (default: the directory's).

env.description: Environment variables this function reads from `Deno.env`, over the process's own.

permissions.description: The worker's permissions (`Deno.PermissionOptions`, e.g. `{ net: true, env: true, read: false }`); by default the worker has the server's. Needs Deno's worker options: list `"worker-options"` in `deno.json`'s `unstable` (the plugin refuses to start otherwise — without it Deno would exit the process on the first request).

vault.description: Vault: secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM in the app (key: `DENEXT_VAULT_KEY`) and stored in `vault.secrets`, Supabase Vault's table shape — `vault` from `@denext/backend/server`. Needs `postgres`.

key.description: The encryption key (default `DENEXT_VAULT_KEY`): at least 32 characters (a random 32-byte value, base64-encoded, is ideal). A list rotates keys: the first encrypts, every one decrypts.

migrate.description: Apply the `backend_vault_0001` migration on first use (default `true`).

sql.description: Supabase's SQL surface too: `vault.create_secret()`, `vault.update_secret()` and the `vault.decrypted_secrets` view, for SQL and migrations written for Supabase. They read the key from a transaction-local setting the app sets — only in `vault.withKey()` transactions and `denext db push / reset / diff` — so outside those they raise an error. Needs `pgcrypto`. See the docs for what this mode trusts the database session with.

queues.description: Queues with pgmq's SQL API (no extension) and Supabase's `pgmq_public` wrappers — `queue()`, `queues` and `queueConsumer()` from `@denext/backend/server`. Needs `postgres`.

migrate.description: Apply the `backend_queues_0001` migration on first use (default `true`).

webhooks.description: Database webhooks: `supabase_functions.http_request` triggers record changes, and the app delivers them to the configured hooks, signed and retried. Needs `postgres`.

secret.description: The signing secret (`whsec_<base64>` or any string); default: `webhooks.secret`.

headers.description: Headers added to every request (the trigger's own come first; signing headers win).

timeoutMs.description: The request timeout in milliseconds (default: the trigger's, else 5000).

allowUrls.description: URLs a trigger may name directly (Supabase's `http_request('https://…')`): each entry is a URL prefix (`"https://hooks.example.com/"`). Default: none — a URL in a trigger is refused.

maxAttempts.description: Attempts before an event is marked failed (default 8).

backoffMs.description: The first retry's delay in ms, doubled per attempt (default 10 000).

maxBackoffMs.description: The longest retry delay in ms (default 3 600 000).

pollIntervalMs.description: How often the deliverer looks for due events, in ms (default 5000; NOTIFY wakes it sooner).

delivery.description: `"auto"` (default): `denext dev` / `denext start` deliver in the background. `"manual"`: only `deliverWebhooks()` does (from a job, say).

retention.description: How long settled events are kept, in milliseconds from when the change happened: `delivered` ones (default 7 days) and `failed` ones — given up on after `maxAttempts`, or never allowed to go anywhere — (default 30 days). Older ones are deleted by the background deliverer (once an hour) and by `purgeWebhookEvents()` / `webhookCleanupJob()`. `false` keeps every event.

migrate.description: Apply the `backend_webhooks_*` migrations on first use (default `true`).

plugins.name: @denext/content-collections
plugins.title: @denext/content-collections
plugins.blurb: A typed, validated, queryable content layer for denext apps — MD/MDX/YAML/JSON, in the spirit of Astro's Content Layer and Nuxt Content.

watch.description: Glob patterns (relative to the project root) whose changes regenerate the store + types in `denext dev`. Defaults to `content.config.ts` and a `content/**` tree; override if your content lives elsewhere.

markdown.description: How `<Content>` / `renderContent` render raw HTML in `.md` entries: `{ html: "escape" }` (the default) shows it as text; `{ html: "sanitize", sanitize?: { allowElements, allowAttributes, allowDataImages } }` keeps what denext's allowlist sanitizer allows (GitHub's element set; no scripts, styles, frames, forms, SVG/MathML, event handlers or script URLs, whatever is listed). Stored with each `.md` entry at build; a `renderContent` call's own `markdown` overrides it. `.mdx` entries are unaffected.

html.description: Raw HTML in the source: `"escape"` (the default) shows it as text; `"sanitize"` keeps what the allowlist sanitizer allows (see sanitizeHtml) and drops the rest.

sanitize.description: With `html: "sanitize"`: additions to the sanitizer's built-in allowlist.

allowElements.description: More element names to keep (lower-case HTML names such as `"center"`).

allowAttributes.description: More attributes to keep, keyed by element name, or `"*"` for every element — for example `{ "*": ["class"] }` keeps `class` (stripped by default) everywhere. A URL-bearing attribute (`href`, `src`, `cite`, `poster`, …) is still scheme-checked.

allowDataImages.description: Keep `data:image/(png|gif|jpeg|webp);base64,…` URLs, on `` only (never SVG). Default `false`.

plugins.blurb: The offline denext documentation corpus behind denext mcp's denext_search_docs and denext_read_docs tools: every page of the denext docs site chunked by heading, the root guides, every example's…

plugins.name: @denext/effect
plugins.title: @denext/effect
plugins.blurb: First-class Effect support for denext. Run an Effect from a Server Component, route handler, or Server Action and get typed errors, dependency injection (services from a Layer), structured…

layer.description: An app `Layer` providing the services your Effects require (its requirements must be `never`). The plugin builds a memoized runtime from it and disposes it on shutdown; the ambient runEffect/runEffectExit then resolve those services at run time.

plugins.name: @denext/graphql
plugins.title: @denext/graphql
plugins.blurb: A GraphQL endpoint for a denext app, as a plugin. It mounts a GraphQL Yoga server at /graphql, bridges subscriptions onto denext channels (the app's push primitive — no second event bus), serves them…

path.description: Where the endpoint is mounted (default `/graphql`, app-relative: `basePath` is already stripped).

graphiql.description: Serve GraphiQL on a browser `GET` (default: dev only).

introspection.description: Answer introspection queries (default: dev only — production hides the type graph).

maxBodyBytes.description: Max request body in bytes (default 1 MiB, like a route handler; over → 413).

maxConnections.description: Open subscription connections — WebSockets plus streamed (SSE / multipart) responses — across every client; past it a new one is refused with `429` before the upgrade or the response. Default: the app's `live.limits.maxConnections`, else 10 000 (Live's default).

maxConnectionsPerIp.description: Open subscription connections from one client address, keyed as Live keys its own: `clientIpForLimits({ bucket: true })` — a trusted proxy's hop or the `rateLimitHeader` address, an IPv6 client's /64, and no per-address cap for a loopback/private peer behind an untrusted proxy (`rateLimitLocalAddresses` counts those). Default: the app's `live.limits.maxConnectionsPerIp`, else 64 (Live's default).

maxDepth.description: Reject a query nested deeper than this many selection levels — a cheap guard against the DoS where a small deeply-nested query over a cyclic type relation exhausts CPU/memory (the body cap allows thousands of levels). Default 12; `false` disables it. Raise it for a schema with legitimately deep trees.

maxCost.description: Reject a query whose estimated **cost** exceeds this budget — the guard against the *multiplicative* DoS a depth limit misses: `users(first: 1000) { posts(first: 1000) { … } }` is shallow but fans out to a million resolver calls. Cost is estimated over the AST (no schema or resolver run): each field costs CostOptions.fieldCost (default 1), and a field carrying a pagination argument (`first`/`last`/`limit` by default) multiplies its children's cost by that integer. Default `false` (off — `maxDepth` stays the on-by-default guard); set a number (a budget of ~1000 suits most apps) to enable it. The check runs at execute time, so a page size passed as a **variable** (`first: $n`) is counted at its **actual** value — a variable can't smuggle a large page past the budget. With Yoga `batching` enabled the budget covers the **whole batch**: the operations' costs are summed when the request is parsed, and a batch over the budget is refused (`400`) before any of them runs.

costOptions.description: Tune the GraphqlOptions.maxCost estimate (field weight, which args multiply).

fieldCost.description: Cost charged for each field selected (default `1`).

listMultiplierArgs.description: Argument names whose integer value multiplies a field's subtree cost (default `["first", "last", "limit"]`).

defaultMultiplier.description: Multiplier used for a pagination field when its size is a variable or absent (default `1`).

requireSameOrigin.description: Require the same-origin proof denext applies to every state-changing RPC (Server Actions, the typed-API batch) on non-GET requests: a cross-site `<form>` or fetch is refused with 403 before Yoga parses it. Default `true`. Turn off only for a public, cookie-free API — resolvers run in the viewer's session, so a mutation reached cross-site is a CSRF.

allowedOrigins.description: Extra origins (`https://app.example.com`) allowed to call mutations, beyond the request's own host.

context.description: Build the per-request context your resolvers receive (merged with Yoga's).

yoga.description: Further Yoga options: `plugins`, `maskedErrors`, `cors`, `batching`, `logging`, … Note `cors` defaults to OFF here (Yoga's own default reflects any `Origin` with credentials); set `cors: { origin: [...] }` to open the endpoint to named sites.

outFile.description: The SDL file `denext build` writes into the output directory (default `schema.graphql`); `false` skips it.

websocket.description: Serve GraphQL over WebSocket — the `graphql-ws` protocol (subprotocol `graphql-transport-ws`) — on the same path, next to GraphQL over SSE. On by default; `false` turns it off. The handshake needs a browser `Origin` on the app's own host (or in `allowedOrigins`, or the app's `desktop.app.origin`) unless `requireSameOrigin: false`; the socket's identity is the upgrade request's cookies / `Authorization`, or a `connection_init` payload token (`{ authorization: "Bearer …" }` or `{ token }`) when the upgrade carried no `Authorization`. Every operation passes the same depth / cost limits as over HTTP.

connectionInitTimeoutMs.description: Close a socket that sent no `connection_init` within this many milliseconds (default 3000).

maxSubscriptions.description: Operations one socket may run at once — subscriptions, queries and mutations alike (default 32, Live's per-connection channel cap). Past it a `subscribe` gets an `error` frame.

watch.description: Under `denext dev`, the files whose edit reloads the schema (globs, relative to the project root). Default: the scripts and `.graphql` files in the schema module's directory and below (the schema module alone when it sits at the project root) — the module path given, or the module a schema object / factory was traced to. In-flight subscriptions on the old schema end (`complete`). A schema object that cannot be traced (it is built in `denext.config.ts` itself, or reached through a non-relative import) needs a restart after an edit; a dev notice says so.
