plugins.title: @denext/openapi
plugins.blurb: An OpenAPI 3.1 document and a docs page for a denext app, derived from the defineApi definitions its route handlers already carry.

path.description: Where the document is served (default `/openapi.json`, app-relative: `basePath` is already stripped).

docs.description: Where the docs page is served (default `/docs`, app-relative); `false` disables it.

ui.description: The docs renderer: `builtin` (server-rendered, no JavaScript — the default), `swagger` (interactive Swagger UI, vendored and served from the app's own origin under `<docs>/swagger-ui/`, each file checked against its recorded SHA-256) or `scalar` (interactive Scalar API reference, vendored the same way and served under `<docs>/scalar/`, configured to call none of Scalar's own services). Each page answers with its own strict CSP naming no other origin.

cdn.description: Load `scalar` from a CDN script URL (e.g. `DOCS_CDN.scalar`), or `swagger` from a CDN dist base URL (e.g. `DOCS_CDN.swagger`), instead of the vendored copy. The page's CSP then names that origin.

info.description: The document's `info` (defaults: the project directory's name, version `0.0.0`).

toJsonSchema.description: Describe validators the built-in detection cannot (consulted first).

include.description: Keep a route in the document (default: every API route).

tags.description: Tag an operation (default: the first path segment after `/api`).

securitySchemes.description: Security schemes the document advertises (→ `components.securitySchemes`). Swagger UI and Scalar render an "Authorize" button from these, so a token is entered once and sent with each request. E.g. `{ bearerAuth: { type: "http", scheme: "bearer" } }`.

security.description: Which scheme(s) an operation requires. An **array** is a document-wide default; a **function** is applied per route — return `[{ bearerAuth: [] }]` to require it, `[]` for a public route (e.g. `/api/login`), or `undefined` to leave it at the document default. This is DOCUMENTATION only — enforce the token with route middleware (`createApi().use(...)`).

expose.description: When the live endpoints are served. `"always"` (default) serves `/openapi.json` and `/docs` in every mode — the zero-config default, since a document describing your own API is usually fine to expose. `"dev"` serves them only under `denext dev` (like GraphiQL), so production reveals no route/schema map. Either way authorize still applies.

authorize.description: Gate the live endpoints. Return `false` to hide them from a request (the app's own 404 answers — no distinguishable "forbidden"). Runs after expose. Default: open.

outFile.description: The file `denext build` writes into the output directory (default `openapi.json`); `false` skips the build step.

sources.description: More OpenApiSources to describe beside the app's routes. The sources plugins register themselves (`@denext/backend`'s auto-REST routes) are included without this; `sources: false` leaves every registered one out.

name.description: A unique name (`"@denext/backend rest"`); a later registration under it replaces the earlier.

describe.description: Describe the routes now (called on each document build, so a changed database catalog shows on the next request).

Return a plain object (its properties are `context.x`) or a `RouterContextProvider` (`context.get(key)`); with none, each request starts with an empty `RouterContextProvider`. plugins.name: @denext/tanstack-start
plugins.title: @denext/tanstack-start
plugins.blurb: Run a TanStack Start app on denext, through the plugin-kit seams alone: server functions, server routes, streamed pages, hydration, Start's import protection and its prerender.

srcDirectory.description: The source directory, relative to the project (default `src`).

router.description: The router module, relative to `srcDirectory` (default `router.tsx`), or Start's own `router` option: `{ entry, basepath, ...the route generator's options }`. `entry` may leave out the extension; `basepath` must match the app's `basePath`; the generator's options (`routesDirectory` and `generatedRouteTree` relative to `srcDirectory`, as in Start) apply over `tsr.config.json`.

entry.description: The router module, relative to `srcDirectory`; the extension may be left out (default `router`, as in Start).

basepath.description: The router's base path. It must match the app's `basePath` (denext serves the app under that); set `basePath` in `denext.config.ts` instead.

maxBodyBytes.description: The request-body cap for server functions and server routes, in bytes; a larger body is a 413 before Start sees it. Default: the app's `actionMaxBodyBytes`, else 1 MiB.

allowedOrigins.description: Origins (`https://app.example.com`) or bare hosts allowed to call a server function with a mutating method, on top of the app's own origin.

importProtection.description: Start's `importProtection` options (as `tanstackStart({ importProtection })` takes them in Start's Vite plugin): extra denied specifiers and files per side, the importers checked, `onViolation`, `enabled`, `maxTraceDepth`, `behavior`. As in Start, `behavior` defaults to `"mock"` in `denext dev` and `"error"` in a build. An `"error"` violation fails the build (in dev, the request that builds); a `"mock"` one makes the denied import Start's mock module (`mockAccess` sets its browser diagnostics in dev) and the violation a warning, once per process (`log: "once"`, the default) or on every build (`log: "always"`).

enabled.description: `false` turns Start's import protection off (denext's server-only scan still runs).

client.description: Rules for the browser build (`specifiers` add to Start's; the other lists replace them).

specifiers.description: Import specifiers the environment may not import (matched as written).

files.description: Files (root-relative paths) the environment may not import.

excludeFiles.description: Files exempt from `files` (default: everything under a `node_modules` directory).

server.description: Rules for the server build (each list replaces Start's).

specifiers.description: Import specifiers the environment may not import (matched as written).

files.description: Files (root-relative paths) the environment may not import.

excludeFiles.description: Files exempt from `files` (default: everything under a `node_modules` directory).

include.description: When set, only importers matching one of these (root-relative) are checked.

exclude.description: Importers matching these are not checked.

ignoreImporters.description: Importers matching these are not checked.

onViolation.description: Called for each violation; returning `false` waives it.

behavior.description: Start's violation behavior: `"error"`, `"mock"` (both commands), or one per command (`{ dev, build }`). Unset, or a command the object leaves out, takes Start's default: `"mock"` in `denext dev`, `"error"` in a build (`build`, `start`, `export`). A `"mock"` is Start's: a denied import resolves to Start's mock module, a denied file is replaced by one, and the violation is a warning; an `"error"` fails the build (in dev, the request that builds).

mockAccess.description: Start's runtime diagnostics for a mocked import in the browser (dev `"mock"` only): using the mock logs Start's `[import-protection] Mocked import used in dev client` with `console.error` (`"error"`, the default) or `console.warn` (`"warn"`), or nothing (`"off"`).

maxTraceDepth.description: How many importers a violation's trace walks up at most (default 20, as in Start).

log.description: Start's repetition of its warnings: `"once"` (default) warns about each mocked violation once per process, `"always"` on every build. A violation that fails the build is reported on every build either way.

prerender.description: Start's `prerender` options for `denext export` (on by default there; `enabled: false` exports no TanStack routes).

concurrency.description: How many pages render at once (default: the CPU count).

filter.description: Whether a page is prerendered (a falsy return leaves it out).

failOnError.description: A page that fails fails the export (default `true`).

autoStaticPathsDiscovery.description: Add the route tree's static paths to the pages (default `true`).

pages.description: Start's `pages`: the paths `denext export` prerenders (default `/`, plus discovery).

path.description: The page's path, under the router's base path.

prerender.description: This page's prerender options (over the `prerender` ones).

outputPath.description: Where the page's HTML is written (a path under the export).

crawlLinks.description: Prerender the links the page has (default `true`).

onSuccess.description: Called with each prerendered page; a returned object is merged into the page.

fromCrawl.description: Found by crawling a prerendered page's links.

sitemap.description: Start's `sitemap`: `denext export` writes `sitemap.xml` (at `outputPath`, default `sitemap.xml`) and `pages.json` with Start's own sitemap builder, over every page the prerender met; `host` is required.

enabled.description: `false` writes no sitemap (default `true` once the option is given).

host.description: The site's origin each `<loc>` starts with (required).

outputPath.description: Where the sitemap is written in the export (default `sitemap.xml`).

spa.description: Start's `spa`: `denext export` also renders Start's SPA shell (the root route alone) at `maskPath` (default `/`) to `_shell.html` (`prerender.outputPath`), the file a static host serves for any path the export has no file for. In `denext dev`, as in Start's dev server, every page renders as the shell and the browser renders the route (`enabled: false` turns both off).

enabled.description: `false` writes no shell (default `true` once the option is given).

maskPath.description: The URL the shell is rendered at (default `/`).

prerender.description: The shell page's prerender options (default `outputPath: "/_shell"`, no crawling).

outputPath.description: Where the page's HTML is written (a path under the export).

crawlLinks.description: Prerender the links the page has (default `true`).

onSuccess.description: Called with each prerendered page; a returned object is merged into the page.
